item: The custody log follows the post-quantum half of its signing key through rotation records (open-on-main rows 42-44)
key_paths: src/custody/log.py; scripts/verify_custody.py; docs/SECURITY.md; docs/USER_MANUAL.md; tests/test_custody_pqc_rotation.py; tests/test_custody_key_rotation.py
summary: Rows 42-44. A change of the ML-DSA half alone (post-quantum signing turned on or off, its key re-created) wrote no key-rotation record, so a pinned check refused the honest log; it now writes one, signed by the same Ed25519 key and passed by name. Every new record names the whole previous identity: its endorsement binds the previous ML-DSA key and must carry it (an endorsement with another or a stripped post-quantum half is refused), and in a whole log the entry before the record must be signed with it. Under --pin a head stripped to its Ed25519 half under a signer that names an ML-DSA key is refused, and so is an Ed25519-only entry in any stretch a new record introduced; a stretch no new record covers keeps the old tolerance so logs written before 0.5.1 still verify. Older checkers refuse a log with an ML-DSA-only record (fail closed).
